**Park Ji‑sung** (박지성) is a retired South Korean professional footballer who played primarily as a midfielder. He was born on **April 8, 1981** in Seoul, South Korea.

### Career Highlights

| Period | Club | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| 1999–2000 | Suwon Samsung Bluewings (K League) | Started his professional career in South Korea. |
| 2000–2005 | PSV Eindhoven (Netherlands) | Became a key player in the Eredivisie, winning the league in 2004–05. |
| 2005–2012 | Manchester United (Premier League) | Joined in 2005 for a then club record fee. Won three Premier League titles, the FA Cup, the League Cup, the UEFA Champions League (2007–08), and the FIFA Club World Cup. Known for his work‑rate, stamina, and versatility. |
| 2012–2014 | FC Tokyo (J1 League) | Returned to Asia, helping the club win the J.League Cup in 2012. |
| 2014–2015 | Ulsan Hyundai (K League) | Finished his playing career in his home country. |

### International Career

- Represented South Korea at the **2002 FIFA World Cup**, where the team reached the semi‑finals (the “Miracle of Doha”).
- Earned **108 caps** for the national team, scoring 12 goals.
- Played in the **2004, 2007, 2010, and 2014 FIFA World Cups** and the **2006, 2010, and 2014 Asian Cups**.

### Playing Style & Reputation

- Nicknamed “The Iron Man” for his relentless energy and ability to cover large areas of the pitch.
- Known for his powerful left foot, precise passing, and tactical intelligence.
- Highly respected for his professionalism, humility, and leadership both on and off the field.

### Post‑Retirement

- After retiring in 2015, Park has been involved in various football-related activities, including coaching roles, ambassadorial duties, and media appearances.
- He has also pursued interests outside football, such as music and business ventures.

Park Ji‑sung remains one of South Korea’s most celebrated footballers and is widely regarded as a role model for aspiring athletes in the country.
